::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** June 13th 1857  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS University of Delaware Library, Newark, Delaware, F295
:::

My dear [Miss Butler](people/person_237.qmd),
Two lines to say that here I am at home, & shall be delighted to have [Likes & Dislikes](other_books/otherbook_248.qmd) if they are ready. I go to [Dogd](organizations/other_121.qmd) on Monday week, but if I could have them in the interval, I should be glad. But I am afraid it is of  no use to try for two chapters in [one number](organizations/other_52.qmd) I am engaged to so much, I have been reading Peothès[^1] in English and delighting in him.

In great haste
Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The librarian confirms that the word looks like Peothes, but no explanation can be offered.
